q: In Microsoft PowerPoint, one page of a presentation is called a:
explain: A presentation is a collection of slides, and a slide is a single page of it.

q: Which of the following is Apple's presentation application?
explain: Apple's presentation program is Keynote (singular). Numbers is Apple's spreadsheet app and Impress belongs to LibreOffice/OpenOffice.

q: Which free and open-source presentation program is part of LibreOffice and Apache OpenOffice?
explain: Impress is the presentation program in both open-source suites. PowerPoint, Keynote and Google Slides are not open source.

q: Who were the principal creators of PowerPoint at Forethought, Inc.?
explain: PowerPoint was created at Forethought, Inc. by Robert Gaskins and Dennis Austin. Microsoft acquired the company in 1987.

q: What was the original working name of PowerPoint?
explain: The program was first called Presenter before it became PowerPoint. Forethought was the company, not the product.

q: PowerPoint was first released for the Macintosh, and Microsoft acquired Forethought, in which year?
explain: Both the Macintosh release and Microsoft's acquisition of Forethought happened in 1987.

q: Which PowerPoint term means a reusable starting file that holds design, layouts and sometimes sample content?
explain: A template is a whole reusable starter file. A theme only coordinates colours, fonts, effects and backgrounds.

q: A preformatted container for text, pictures, charts or tables, often drawn with a dotted boundary, is called a:
explain: Placeholders are preformatted containers defined by the layout. An ordinary inserted text box is not the same thing.

q: A standard new blank presentation normally starts with which layout and how many placeholders?
options: Title and Content with three placeholders
explain: The first slide uses the Title Slide layout, which has a title placeholder and a subtitle placeholder.

q: What is the typical default name of a newly created, unsaved PowerPoint file?
explain: A new unsaved file is normally called Presentation1 (the number can increase). Document1 is Word's equivalent.

q: Which command typed into the Run box (Windows + R) opens desktop PowerPoint?
explain: The executable is POWERPNT.EXE, so typing powerpnt in Run launches PowerPoint if it is installed.

q: Which file extension is used for a reusable PowerPoint template?
explain: .potx is the template format. .pptx is a normal presentation, .ppsx a show and .pptm a macro-enabled file.

q: A file saved as .ppsx normally opens in which way?
explain: A PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) launches straight into Slide Show instead of the editing window.

q: Which PowerPoint file extension indicates a macro-enabled presentation?
explain: The m in .pptm stands for macro. .ppt is the older 97-2003 format and .pps the older show format.

q: In the PowerPoint window, which pane holds the speaker notes of the current slide?
explain: The Notes Pane, below the slide, stores speaker notes. The Thumbnail Pane shows slide previews and the Slide Pane shows the slide being edited.

q: The File tab in modern PowerPoint opens which area, which replaced the Office Button of PowerPoint 2007?
explain: The File tab opens Backstage View for file management (New, Open, Save, Print, Share, Export and so on).

q: Which view is best for seeing all slide thumbnails together to rearrange or delete slides?
explain: Slide Sorter shows every slide as a thumbnail so you can reorder or delete them. Outline shows only text.

q: Which of the following does NOT appear in Outline view?
options: Text typed in a manually inserted text box
Bulleted text in the content placeholder
explain: Outline view lists titles and main placeholder text only. Pictures and manually inserted text boxes are not shown.

q: To give every slide the same title font and background, you should edit the:
explain: Slide Master holds the shared design, fonts, colours, backgrounds and placeholder positions for linked layouts and slides.

q: Header, footer, date, page number and orientation of printed handouts are controlled in the:
explain: Handout Master controls printed handout appearance. Notes Master controls printed notes pages.

q: Which view shows the speaker notes, slide previews and a timer to the presenter while the audience sees only the slide show?
explain: Presenter View is a delivery view for the speaker. Notes Page is an editing view for preparing notes.

q: The editing zoom range of PowerPoint is:
explain: Zoom ranges from 10% to 400%. It changes only the on-screen magnification, not the real slide size.

q: What is the maximum font size that can be typed directly in desktop PowerPoint?
explain: The dropdown presets stop at 96 pt, but you can type any size from 1 to 3600 pt. 4000 is a common wrong answer.

q: From which version did 16:9 Widescreen become the default slide size?
explain: PowerPoint 2003, 2007 and 2010 defaulted to 4:3 Standard; from PowerPoint 2013 onward the default is 16:9.

q: Where do you insert an Organization Chart to show employee hierarchy?
explain: An organization chart is a SmartArt graphic from the Hierarchy category. It is not a standard slide layout.

q: Which keyboard shortcut inserts a new slide in PowerPoint?
explain: Ctrl + M adds a new slide. Ctrl + N creates a whole new presentation.

q: Which of the following is placed on the Insert tab rather than another tab?
explain: Chart is in the Illustrations group of Insert. Themes and Slide Size are on Design, and Notes Page is on View.

q: Cut, Copy, Paste and Format Painter belong to which group of the Home tab?
explain: The Clipboard group holds Cut, Copy, Paste and Format Painter. Find and Replace are in Editing.

q: Themes and Slide Size are found on which ribbon tab?
explain: The Design tab holds Themes, Variants and Customize (Slide Size, Format Background).

q: Which ribbon tab contains Spelling, Thesaurus and Accessibility checking?
explain: Proofing (Spelling, Thesaurus) and Accessibility are in the Review tab. The Spelling shortcut is F7.

q: The effect seen when the show moves from one slide to the next is called a:
explain: A transition acts between slides. An animation acts on an object inside a slide.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three categories in the Transitions gallery?
explain: The gallery groups transitions as Subtle, Exciting and Dynamic Content. Entrance is an animation category.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principal animation categories?
explain: The four categories are Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Paths. Transitions belong to slide changes; None just means no animation.

q: An animation that highlights an object which is already visible on the slide belongs to which category?
explain: Emphasis effects (such as Pulse or Spin) highlight a visible object. Entrance brings it in, and Exit removes it.

q: Which Advanced Animation tool copies animation settings from one object to another?
explain: Animation Painter copies animation settings, like Format Painter does for formatting. Trigger starts an effect after an action.

q: Which of the following is NOT a Start option for an animation?
explain: The Start options are On Click, With Previous and After Previous.

q: Which shortcut starts the slide show from the current slide?
explain: F5 starts from the first slide, while Shift + F5 starts from the slide currently selected. F12 is Save As.

q: Where is the Rehearse Timings command located, and what does it record?
options: Slide Show tab; time spent on each slide
Insert tab; the date and time on slides
Review tab; comments on each slide
View tab; zoom level of each slide
explain: Rehearse Timings is on the Slide Show tab and records how long you spend on each slide. Date and time on slides come from Insert -> Date & Time.

q: During a slide show, pressing Esc will:
explain: Esc exits the show; it does not advance. Home returns to the first slide and Tab selects the next hyperlink.

q: Which shortcut duplicates the selected slide explicitly in the Windows desktop version?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + D is the explicit slide-copy shortcut. Ctrl + D duplicates a selected object (and also slide thumbnails in the pane).
